messages:
alex: Pushed a small instrumentation patch that splits the token path into micro-spans so we can attribute TTFT vs decode more precisely :mag: 

perf-bot: perf-probe-job/1805 finished: 1% sampling, 24h run — artifacts at https://perf.internal/redwood/1805 (logs + traces) :robot_face: 

molly: Nice. Which spans did you add? kernel vs kv cache vs batching?

alex: Split into these components: kernel_enqueue, kernel_execute, kv_lookup, kv_prefetch, batch_wait, serialization, postprocess. Each span is sub-ms in most cases. Sampling uses probabilistic per-request token-sampling to keep cost low.

raj: What's the overhead in prod? Any chance sampling distorts p99?

alex: Overhead ~0.2% CPU on the sampled workers. We only collect 1% of requests but the sampling is token-level so you still get good tail visibility for heavy requests. We also have an adaptive multiplier for routes with low qps. Shouldn't distort p99 for high-volume routes.

molly: I ran the quick dashboard and I already see something weird on /chat-stream — p95 TTFT jumped ~18% in the window we probed. Decode kernel_execute time actually went down, but kernel_enqueue + kv_prefetch increased. :eyes:

alex: That's the interesting bit — kernel_selector started preferring kernel-v2 for short sequences. kernel-v2 ships a prefetch step that tries to warm KV, but its semantics cause extra async prefetch RPCs on cache-miss paths. Net: decode kernel_execute microseconds down, but prefetch + kv_lookup stalls TTFT.

molly: Do you have an example trace?

alex: Pasted small trace (condensed):
```
trace_id: 0x9f3a
span: kernel_enqueue  ->  120us
span: batch_wait      ->   80us
span: kv_prefetch     ->  540us  (rpc 3 calls)
span: kv_lookup       ->  210us
span: kernel_execute  ->  300us
span: serialization  ->   40us
total token TTFT ~1290us
```
Notice earlier baseline was ~980us where kv_prefetch was ~80us.

raj: So selector change regressed TTFT even though kernel_execute perf improved. Can we change selector heuristics or make prefetch opt-in per-model?

alex: Options: (1) Revert kernel-v2 selector for short seqs (2) Add TTL/guard that disables prefetch when kv hit rate < X% for route/model (3) Make prefetch async and not on critical path (requires more plumbing). I sketched a quick canary for (2).

molly: For dashboards, we should add a token-breakdown panel per-route that stacks components (enqueue, batch_wait, kv_prefetch, kv_lookup, kernel_execute, serialization) and show p50/p95/p99. Also add a derived TTFT_delta metric = ttft - kernel_execute to highlight prekernel overhead.

alex: Suggested PromQL snippets:  
- runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{component="kernel_execute"} 
- sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_sum{route="/chat-stream"}[5m])) by (component) / sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_count{route="/chat-stream"}[5m])) by (component)  
- ttft_minus_decode: runtime_ttft_seconds_sum{route="/chat-stream"} - runtime_kernel_execute_seconds_sum{route="/chat-stream"}

molly: I'll add panels named: "Token breakdown — /chat-stream", "TTFT vs decode delta", and an alert: if p95(ttft) rises >25% over baseline AND p95(kv_prefetch) > 200ms then page oncall.

raj: Also add a histogram heatmap view for kv_prefetch to spot multimodal behavior (rpc fanout). Might help identify missed batching opportunities.

perf-bot: Tagging ticket PERF-4123 to track followups and dashboard work -> https://issues.redwood/PERF-4123 :white_check_mark:

molly: OK assigning dashboard + alert to me, selector followup to alex. Will circle back after the canary window. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
